wo_journey_logs.answers: What stage is work order WO-20240427093000 currently in, and which milestones have been completed? | How long did the actual work take compared to the estimated duration for a given work order?
wo_journey_logs.grain: one work order's journey through its lifecycle stages, from initiation through completion
wo_journey_logs.purpose: This table records the step-by-step progression and state of a work order as it moves through approval, preparation, execution, and closure. It captures milestones reached, timeline expectations versus actuals, assigned technician and team details, cost tracking, and quality metrics.

wo_status_history.answers: When did this work order move from pending_approval to active? | Who approved this work order and when?
wo_status_history.grain: One status transition event for one work order.
wo_status_history.purpose: This table records the complete audit trail of work order lifecycle changes—from creation through closure—capturing who changed the status, when, and why.

work_order_assets.answers: Which assets are included in this work order? | What work orders have touched this asset?
work_order_assets.grain: one asset assigned to one work order
work_order_assets.purpose: This table records which assets are involved in or affected by each work order. It links work orders to the specific equipment, systems, or building components that maintenance or repairs target, enabling tracking of asset-level work history and maintenance dependencies.

work_order_attachments.answers: What files or photos have been uploaded for this work order? | Who uploaded this attachment and when?
work_order_attachments.grain: one file or document attached to a work order or work order task
work_order_attachments.purpose: This table stores references to files, documents, and media uploaded in relation to work orders and their individual tasks. It tracks what was uploaded, by whom, and when, linking attachments to either the overall work order or a specific task within it.

work_order_comments.answers: What notes or updates were added to this work order? | Who commented on this work order and when?
work_order_comments.grain: one comment or note attached to one work order
work_order_comments.purpose: This table records the audit trail and communication history for work orders, capturing what was discussed, decided, or observed during execution.

work_order_history.answers: When did this work order move from 'pending' to 'in progress'? | Who changed the status of this work order, and what notes did they leave?
work_order_history.grain: one status change event on one work order
work_order_history.purpose: This table records the audit trail of work order lifecycle transitions—when a work order moved from one status to another, who made the change, and when.

work_order_parts.answers: What parts were used to complete work order WO-20240401080000? | Which parts have active warranty coverage and until when?
work_order_parts.grain: one spare part consumed or fitted during one work order on one asset
work_order_parts.purpose: This table records which spare parts were used to complete maintenance work orders, including the quantity, cost, and installation date. It links work orders to the specific parts drawn from inventory and installed on assets, and tracks warranty coverage for parts that were fitted.

work_order_resources.purpose: Labour or equipment resources booked onto a work order. Empty.

work_order_statuses.answers: What statuses are available for work orders in our organization? | Which statuses count as 'closed' or completed for reporting purposes?
work_order_statuses.grain: one work order status definition within an organization
work_order_statuses.purpose: This table defines the lifecycle states that work orders can occupy—such as Open, In Progress, On Hold, Completed, or Cancelled. Each organization maintains its own set of status definitions, allowing customization of workflow stages.

work_order_tasks.answers: What tasks make up this work order, and what is the status of each? | Who is assigned to this task, and when was it completed?
work_order_tasks.grain: one discrete task within a work order
work_order_tasks.purpose: This table breaks down work orders into individual tasks, each with its own assignment, status, and time tracking. It connects a work order to its component activities, allowing facilities teams to manage and monitor progress on specific work items rather than treating each order as a monolith.

work_order_users.answers: Who is assigned to this work order? | How many hours has a specific technician spent on a work order?
work_order_users.grain: one user assigned to one work order, with time tracking
work_order_users.purpose: Records which staff members are assigned to each work order and tracks hours they spend on it. Links work orders to the users table to identify technicians, supervisors, or other personnel involved in completing maintenance or repair tasks.

work_orders.answers: What work orders are currently active or blocked on a given asset or building? | Which work orders are overdue or approaching their scheduled date?
work_orders.grain: one maintenance or repair task assigned to a specific asset at a location
work_orders.purpose: This table records all work orders—corrective repairs, planned maintenance, and inspections—issued against assets across your portfolio. It tracks who requested the work, which technician or vendor is assigned, scheduling and cost estimates, approval status, and completion details.

workbook_extras_runs.purpose: One row per migration run: whether the workbook's extra sheets (contract terms, invoice lines, telemetry) were applied after the migration, and with what counts.
